messages:
julia: noticed a nasty p95 east-west jump during the 09:45 batching ramp in us-west-2-prod. p95 went from ~9ms to ~110-140ms for ~7min. graphs: https://grafana/redwood/cluster/us-west-2

kai: saw that too, alerts fired. any recent infra changes in that rack/az? :eyes:

samir: we rolled a NIC driver update to a subset of ml-nodes in rack-r09 overnight (driver v2.4.7 -> v2.5.0). only 7 nodes. no ToR changes scheduled AFAIK.

linh: infra-alert-bot showed a burst of retransmits + a small increase in RDMA QP retries. attaching quick ib stats snapshot:
```
ibdev0: port 1: pkey violations 0, retry cnt 2, rc drops 3
eth0: rx_errors 12 tx_errors 0 rx_dropped 4
```

julia: tcpdump from one of the affected pods shows lots of ICMP frag needed msgs right at the window start. suspect MTU/PMTU issue or offload weirdness.

kai: timeline: driver roll -> 02:15, nightly autoscaler spin -> 03:30, spike at 09:45. wonder if traffic consolidation during peak batching exposed an MTU blackhole.

samir: could also be GRO/TSO interactions on newer driver. had a previous case where GRO + RDMA offloads caused skewed coalescing and bursts.

linh: quick check: on one affected host:
```
# ip link show dev eth0
3: eth0: mtu 9000 qlen 1000 state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
# ethtool -k eth0 | grep gro
generic-receive-offload: on
large-receive-offload: on
```
No obvious MTU mismatch locally. need ToR counters.

infra-alert-bot: ALERT: e2w_p95_latency_us-west-2 >= 120ms (7m) - affected nodes: ml-r09-[02,04,06,08] - incident id inc-2026-2133

noah: marking this as an incident and will page networking. suggested immediate mitigations: 1) enable per-host GRO disable on affected hosts 2) capture full tcpdump + ibv_rcinfo 3) route some batch traffic to other racks to reduce burst.

julia: started rolling disable of GRO on ml-r09-02/04 as a canary: `sudo ethtool -K eth0 gro off gso off tso off`

samir: rolled back driver on one canary node (ml-r09-02) to v2.4.7 -> initial p95 dropped back to ~12ms within 30s. interesting.

kai: ok that's a strong signal. can we test at scale? if driver is culprit we should freeze the driver on remaining nodes and coordinate with networking for ToR rollback plan if needed.

linh: capturing pcap from both ends and switch counters. asked network to dump ToR logs for p9. also running `ibv_devinfo -v` to check firmware mismatches.

noah: action items: samir + ops to plan driver rollover to revert v2.5.0 on the 7 nodes, network to validate ToR MTU & drop counters, julia to track client tail latency and throttles, linchpin: keep batching window throttled for next 2h. I'll update inc-2026-2133. :thumbsup:

julia: FYI after rollback + GRO off on canary, batch tails normalized. continuing roll and monitoring. will post final RCA when we have switch logs. :white_check_mark:
